views.label: Business event round trip
views.note: A use-case event, e.g. Save or Load: Presenter calls the Interactor, then formats its result into a view model.

views.label: Navigation event
views.note: A navigation event, e.g. open detail or back: Presenter asks the Router, which builds and shows the next module.

views.label: Save then dismiss
views.note: Navigation can follow a result: the Interactor saves, and on success the Presenter, not the Interactor, asks the Router to dismiss.

views.label: Result from next module
views.note: The next module hands its outcome, e.g. a picked Payee, back to this Presenter through a delegate or callback.

cards.title: V: View
items: The screen: labels, buttons, lists, forms
Passive: it renders exactly what the Presenter hands it
Reports taps and typing as events, e.g. 'Save tapped'
Holds no state it could not redraw from the view model
Easy to swap or test with a fake Presenter

cards.title: I: Interactor
items: One use case per method, e.g. 'add a transaction'
Applies business rules: validation, totals, balances
Reads and saves data through Entities and storage
Returns plain results, never display text
No UI imports, so it tests without a screen

cards.title: P: Presenter
items: The coordinator for one screen
Decides per event: a use case goes to the Interactor, navigation to the Router
Formats results: dates, currency, empty states, errors
Pushes a ready-to-draw view model to the View
May navigate after a result, e.g. dismiss once a save succeeds

cards.title: E: Entity
items: The core domain objects, e.g. Account, Transaction, Money
Plain data with simple invariants, no persistence code
Passed between Interactors and storage
Know nothing about screens, flows or the Presenter
Stay stable while the UI changes around them

cards.title: R: Router
items: Also called the Wireframe: owns how screens connect
Creates the next module's View, Presenter and Interactor and wires them
Presents, pushes and dismisses from this module's View
Passes data in, and hands results back to the Presenter via a delegate
Keeps modules decoupled: only the Router knows its neighbours
